clue.text: Grabbing glimpse of decisive victory, punch cheat

indicators.note: a punch that is grabbing something holds it inside, so the other letters sit within it
a glimpse is only a brief first look, so just the opening letter of the next word is kept

blocks.note: a hook is a curving punch in boxing
the first letter of decisive
a win is a victory

explanation.surface: A boxer lands a cheating punch just as a decisive victory comes into view.
explanation.definitionFit: To hoodwink someone is to deceive or trick them, which is what a cheat does.

clue.text: Tramp primarily has overpowering personal whiff

indicators.note: primarily means in the first place, so only the leading letter of each of the next two words is taken

blocks.note: the first letters of has and overpowering
BO is body odour, a personal smell

explanation.surface: A vagrant is noticed mainly for a strong personal smell.
explanation.walkthrough: BO, short for body odour, is a standard abbreviation solvers meet often.
explanation.definitionFit: A hobo is a homeless wandering person, the same as a tramp in the noun sense.

clue.text: Unconfined tapir chasing fine animal

indicators.note: unconfined means released from its boundaries, so the word loses its outer letters and keeps the middle
chasing means following behind, so this piece comes after the next one in a down entry

blocks.note: OK means fine or all right
tapir without its first and last letters

explanation.surface: An escaped tapir pursues some fine creature around a zoo.
explanation.walkthrough: The okapi is a central African forest animal related to the giraffe, fittingly next to a tapir in the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: An okapi is a striped forest mammal of Congo, so it is an example of an animal.

clue.text: Have whittled fragments — that’s annoying

indicators.note: fragments are broken pieces, so the letters before it are smashed up and reassembled

blocks.note: the twelve letters taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone whittling wood is left with only bits and grumbles in frustration.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is an exclamation of irritation or exasperation, said when something bothers you.

clue.text: Fixed trouble in elevated study

indicators.note: elevated means raised up, and in a down entry a word read upwards runs backwards
in places one piece inside the other

blocks.note: a den is a private study room
to ail is to trouble or afflict

explanation.surface: Some problem in an upstairs study has been sorted out.
explanation.definitionFit: Nailed means fastened with nails, so fixed in place, and also colloquially solved or done perfectly.

clue.text: Unlimited information relating to The Listener?

indicators.note: unlimited means without its limits, so the outermost letters of the word are removed

blocks.note: information is notice, here losing its first and last letters

explanation.surface: It reads like a note about boundless news concerning The Listener, a former magazine.
explanation.walkthrough: The Listener is also a famous crossword series and a defunct BBC magazine, so the capitals disguise that a listener is simply someone using their ears.
explanation.definitionFit: Otic is the medical adjective for things concerning the ear, the organ a listener hears with.

clue.text: Got temperature wearing hairpiece

blocks.note: T is the abbreviation for temperature
someone wearing a wig is wigged

explanation.surface: Someone caught a fever while sporting a toupee.
explanation.walkthrough: To twig is informal British for to grasp or realise; 'Got' here means understood, as in 'I got the joke'.
explanation.definitionFit: Twigged and got both mean understood or cottoned on, in their informal senses.

clue.text: Sticking together recent changes about erected house

indicators.note: changes means alters, so the letters of the preceding word are rearranged
erected means set upright, and in a down entry reading upward runs the letters backwards
about means around, so the shuffled letters go round the other piece

blocks.note: taken as written
HO is a standard abbreviation for house

explanation.surface: Recent alterations to a newly built house keep it all in one piece.
explanation.definitionFit: Coherent literally means cohering, that is holding together as a single connected mass.

clue.text: Song from dreadful egoists, maybe

indicators.note: dreadful means in a terrible state, so the letters that follow are jumbled into a new order

blocks.note: the letters taken as written

explanation.surface: A tune comes from some dreadful self-obsessed people, perhaps.
explanation.walkthrough: 'As Time Goes By' is the song played by Sam in the film Casablanca; 'maybe' looks like a hedge but supplies letters.
explanation.definitionFit: The title names a famous popular standard from 1931, so it is an example of a song.

clue.text: Excellent lingerie, very alluring up-front

indicators.note: up front means at the very start, so only the opening letter of that word is used

blocks.note: a bra is an item of lingerie
V is the abbreviation for very
the first letter of alluring

explanation.surface: It sounds like a shop assistant praising some appealing underwear.
explanation.definitionFit: Brava is the cry of praise shouted at a female performer, an exclamation meaning well done or splendid.

clue.text: Tip with change, having no time at all for port

indicators.note: having no time at all means every instance of the time abbreviation is dropped, not just one

blocks.note: taken as written
to switch is to change

explanation.surface: Someone leaves a tip with their loose coins, rushing to catch a boat.
explanation.walkthrough: Both T letters go, one from each piece. Ipswich is a town in Suffolk, eastern England, on the Orwell estuary.
explanation.definitionFit: Ipswich is a historic harbour town on an estuary in Suffolk, so it is an example of a port.

clue.text: Digital outlier that’s manually located?

blocks.note: surface reading: something remote in the digital, computing world, located by hand rather than automatically
setter's reading: the digit standing at the far edge, positioned on the hand

explanation.walkthrough: 'Digital' means relating to fingers, and 'manually' means of the hand, not done by hand.
explanation.definitionFit: The smallest digit sits at the outer edge of the hand, so it is the outlying one of the hand's fingers.

clue.text: Hero sussed most of you out

indicators.note: most of means nearly all, so the final letter of that word is cut
out means disordered or wrong, so the collected letters are rearranged

blocks.note: taken as written
you without its last letter

explanation.surface: A hero worked out most of who you are.
explanation.walkthrough: Sussed is British slang for figured out.
explanation.definitionFit: Odysseus is the hero of Homer's Odyssey, the Greek king who spent ten years voyaging home from Troy.

clue.text: Book van, going back round Northern Ireland

indicators.note: going back means travelling in the opposite direction, so the word is read from end to start
round means encircling, so the reversed word wraps the abbreviation

blocks.note: the van is the front or lead position, as in vanguard
NI is the standard abbreviation for Northern Ireland

explanation.surface: Someone reserves a removal van to drive back to Northern Ireland.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Book' looks like a verb meaning reserve, but it is the definition; van means the front, not a vehicle.
explanation.definitionFit: Daniel is a book of the Old Testament, named after the prophet thrown into the lions' den.

clue.text: Threadbare Italian city embraces saint

indicators.note: embraces means holds in its arms, so the city name encloses the abbreviation

blocks.note: Naples is a city in southern Italy
S is the abbreviation for saint

explanation.surface: A shabby Italian city welcomes a holy figure into its arms.
explanation.definitionFit: Nap is the raised surface fibre of cloth; fabric worn so smooth it has lost that pile is threadbare.

clue.text: Introduction of soft metal with nickel backing

indicators.note: backing means moving rearwards, so the abbreviation is read in reverse

blocks.note: lead is a famously soft heavy metal
Ni is the chemical symbol for nickel

explanation.surface: A chemistry note about bringing in a soft metal supported by nickel.
explanation.definitionFit: A lead-in is the opening remarks or material that precedes and introduces the main part of something.

clue.text: Entertaining both sides in election, face refusal

indicators.note: entertaining means hosting a guest, so one piece takes the other inside it
both sides means the two edges, so only the outer letters of that word are taken

blocks.note: a dial is the face of a clock or watch
the first and last letters of election

explanation.surface: A politician who charmed both parties at election time is met with a flat no.
explanation.definitionFit: A denial is a statement refusing to accept or grant something, so it is a form of refusal.

clue.text: What would assess final appeal of criminal computer user

indicators.note: criminal means crooked or wrong, so the letters of the following words are scrambled

blocks.note: the letters taken as written

explanation.surface: A last-ditch legal appeal by a hacker is about to be judged.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Final appeal' looks like a last plea for attractiveness, but it is the last stage of legal appeals.
explanation.definitionFit: A supreme court is the highest court of law, the body that hears and decides a case's last possible appeal.

clue.text: Hard-nosed type that might charge you

definitions.text: Hard-nosed type that might charge you

blocks.note: surface reading: a tough uncompromising person, perhaps a lawyer or tradesman who bills you
setter's reading: a beast with a horny snout that may rush at you

explanation.walkthrough: 'Hard-nosed' is meant literally, a snout bearing horn; 'charge' means rush at, not ask payment.
explanation.definitionFit: The large African or Asian mammal has a horn on its snout and is known to stampede at intruders.

clue.text: There’s unwrapped present

indicators.note: unwrapped means with its outer covering taken off, so the first and last letters go

blocks.note: there's without its first and last letters

explanation.surface: Someone points out an opened gift.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Present' looks like a gift noun, but it is the adjective meaning in attendance.
explanation.definitionFit: To be here is to be in attendance, so it is a synonym of present, as when answering a roll call.

clue.text: Old dons deserve being in media, periodically

indicators.note: being in means sitting inside, so one piece is placed within the other
periodically means at regular intervals, so only every other letter of that word is kept

blocks.note: the second and fourth letters of media
to merit is to deserve

explanation.surface: Elderly academics deserve to appear on television now and then.
explanation.walkthrough: Dons are university lecturers in Britain, especially at Oxford and Cambridge.
explanation.definitionFit: Emeriti are retired professors who keep their title honorarily, so they are former, old academics.

clue.text: Snatch letters, reportedly

indicators.note: reportedly means as people say it, so the answer matches the spoken form of the letters

blocks.note: the plural of the letter C, said out loud

explanation.surface: Someone grabs post as it arrives.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Letters' looks like mail, but it means letters of the alphabet: several Cs.
explanation.definitionFit: To seize is to grab suddenly and forcibly, so it is a direct synonym of snatch as a verb.

clue.text: Window frame needs front of seasoned wood

indicators.note: front of means the leading part, so only the opening letter of that word is used

blocks.note: the first letter of seasoned
ash is a type of timber tree

explanation.surface: A carpenter says a window frame calls for properly dried timber.
explanation.definitionFit: A sash is the framed glazed panel of a window that slides up and down in its grooves.

clue.text: My oracle, unfortunately mine

indicators.note: unfortunately suggests things gone wrong, so the letters before it come out in a different order

blocks.note: the letters taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone laments that the prophet they consult is, sadly, their own.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mine' looks like the possessive, but it is the explosive device.
explanation.definitionFit: A claymore is a directional anti-personnel explosive device, named after the Scottish broadsword, so it is a kind of mine.
